chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kazzaz from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far from his father from Ali (peace be upon him)

In the case of a man who pronounces Zihar from four women, he said: 'Upon him is one expiation.' The meaning in this report is what preceded the statement in similar cases, that we interpret it to mean that upon him is one expiation in kind, either freeing a slave, or fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people, according to the obligatory sequence in that matter. And it is not obligatory for some of them [the women] to have freeing [of a slave], and for some of them fasting, or feeding [the poor]. And the meaning of his saying 'one expiation' is not that one of the expiations suffices for the four women.

key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: Zihar (verbal divorce where husband compares wife to mother's back)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for Zihar if a man pronounces it on multiple wives at once?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that the single expiation mentioned in the hadith refers to the genus of the penalty rather than a single act satisfying all wives simultaneously, thereby avoiding the impracticality of requiring multiple distinct expiations for one pronouncement. This interpretation aligns with the Shia scholarly view that the obligation is singular in nature but applies collectively to the group of wives involved in the simultaneous declaration. The ruling emphasizes the sequential hierarchy of expiation options while maintaining the unity of the legal consequence.
